role: The local player on the client: turns MovementInput into motion, runs sprint double-tap and fly toggles, pushes out of blocks, lags the first-person arm, tracks the portal overlay and opens the GUI screens the server asks for.
scope_reason: The client player's tick produces the movement packets the server tick consumes, so it is part of every replay row.

notes: The GUI-opening methods are marked partial without a symbol because the native screens are driven from gui_screens.c/container.c by the server's S2D window packets rather than through these calls; this was not traced symbol by symbol. The enableEverythingIsScrewedUpMode branch (demo/spectator camera) is not needed. Evidence is the replay2-* walking/sneak/jump snapshots and flow-walk-s1 (DEVLOG line 1058: 0 field mismatches over 303 ticks) run by csrc/tests/test_snapshots.c. lane/idxclient: the portal block's screen close is ported (surv_client_portal_close: displayGuiScreen(null), not closeScreen, so openContainer and the server's window stay; GuiInventory then opens over inventoryContainer, cp_gui_container). idx-portalclose-s1 (a GuiInventory with a cursor stack and grid items closed by a portal; the client's spill draws are proven by an Unbreaking I pickaxe's client-side rolls: one erand draw short fails at row 47; master's native fails at row 33) and idx-portalchest-s1 (a chest opened in the portal: the screen closes the tick it opens, GuiInventory over the stale window, clicks the server drops).
